topic.angle: Small loans to the poor without collateral

panels.text: In 1976 Muhammad Yunus, a professor at the University of Chittagong, launched a research project on how to bring banking services to the rural poor.
It grew into Grameen Bank, founded in Bangladesh. It makes small loans, called microcredit, to poor people without requiring collateral.
Terms are kept reasonable, with group lending and weekly instalments. Around 97% of its members are women.
The bank is owned by its borrowers, most of whom are poor women. In 2006 the bank and Yunus were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

probes.question: What does Grameen Bank not require from the people it lends to?
True or false: Grameen Bank is owned by its borrowers.
